article_ideas.angle: Decompose real failure cases into misattribution, unit scaling, and fabricated arithmetic, then show that only the first responds to retrieval improvements.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers building RAG systems for regulated or mission-critical domains
article_ideas.based_on: A third of all citations in financial tasks are math the model did not actually perform.
article_ideas.thesis: Retrieval accuracy and computational accuracy are independent failure surfaces, and teams conflate them: they invest in embeddings and recall while the system keeps emitting figures it never computed and numbers whose units it silently rescaled. The fix is not better retrieval but a value registry that makes the model a reference emitter rather than a number generator.
article_ideas.title: Your RAG Pipeline Doesn't Have a Retrieval Problem, It Has an Arithmetic Problem

article_ideas.angle: Frame the shift as moving a correctness property from the model's behavior to the system's type system, and be candid about what breaks when the tool surface is incomplete.
article_ideas.audience: Agent and platform architects designing high-stakes generation systems
article_ideas.based_on: The model cites numbers but never writes them.
article_ideas.thesis: Behavioral guardrails (better prompts, polite instructions, self-check passes) are probabilistic and regress with every model swap. Structural guarantees — the model emits plans and references, tools emit values — convert numerical correctness into a type error. The honest trade is coverage brittleness for structural impossibility, and that trade should be made explicitly rather than discovered in production.
article_ideas.title: Make It Unrepresentable: Turning Hallucination Mitigation from Prompting into Type-Checking

article_ideas.angle: Compare enforcement points along the generation pipeline and argue the gate should sit where the user's read happens.
article_ideas.audience: Engineers responsible for production LLM output quality and safety gates
article_ideas.based_on: strips any number that cannot be matched
article_ideas.thesis: Post-hoc verification and offline evaluation audit outputs after the fact and depend on the model behaving as it did when you measured it. Enforcement placed in the output path — validating each value as it is generated and suppressing anything without a registered source — survives model regression, prompt drift, and planner degradation, at the cost of streaming complexity and content loss that must itself be measured.
article_ideas.title: Guardrails Belong in the Token Stream, Not the Eval Suite

article_ideas.angle: Treat cross-document contradiction as a first-class retrieval stage rather than an edge case, with hybrid over-fetch plus fusion plus authority-aware reranking.
article_ideas.audience: Search and retrieval engineers working on enterprise document corpora
article_ideas.based_on: A trusted cross-encoder reranks results to filter out conflicting disclosures
article_ideas.thesis: In real corpora, documents disagree — a transcript and a filing state the same fact differently. Relevance ranking cannot resolve this, because the most similar passage is not the authoritative one. Retrieval pipelines need an explicit arbitration stage where source authority is a modeled input, and the reranker is the natural place to encode it.
article_ideas.title: Rerankers Aren't Just Rankers: Handling Contradictory Sources in Enterprise Corpora

summary.html:
Overview

  • Speaker: Vinoo Ganesh
  • Channel: AI Engineer
  • Main topic: Preventing LLMs from hallucinating numerical data in financial applications using deterministic code, retrieval, and streaming filters.
  • Purpose: To explain Kepler's architecture for verifiable numerical data retrieval, computation, and citation filtering in AI systems. Vinoo Ganesh, CEO of Kepler, presents an architecture and methodology for preventing language models from inventing numbers in mission-critical environments like finance. By separating planning (handled by LLMs) from execution (handled by deterministic code, retrieval, and strict citation registries), Kepler ensures every figure is retrieved, computed, and verified. The talk explores how standard RAG and LLM wrappers fail when dealing with financial data, why a third of citations are often math models fail to do, and five core rules for ensuring verifiable numerical AI systems.

Topic Map

The Problem of Numerical Hallucination in LLMs

  • Explanation: LLMs are probability machines at their core. While this makes them creative, it makes them unreliable for mission-critical numerical tasks like financial analysis where every number must be traceable.
  • Key claims:
    • LLMs do not read documents directly; they chunk text, perform semantic search, and retrieve semi-relevant information.
    • Attaching sources after the fact leads to wrong sources, wrong numbers due to scaling issues, and incorrect mental math.
    • A third of all citations in financial tasks are math the model did not actually perform.
  • Examples:
    • Pulling information from random blogs stating Palantir is worth $100,000 a share.
    • Reading a 10K and confusing the number 17 for millions, billions, yen, or page numbers.
  • Terminology:
    • probability machines
    • post-hoc citation
    • semantic search
  • Why it matters: Financial analysts and enterprise users cannot trust AI outputs that invent or miscalculate critical figures.

Kepler's Architecture: Separation of Planning and Deterministic Software

  • Explanation: Kepler implements an architecture where language models handle planning, while deterministic code handles retrieval, computation, and post-processing verification.
  • Key claims:
    • The model cites numbers but never writes them.
    • Retrieval finds the source, deterministic code does the math, and a post-processing filter checks every receipt.
    • Every number must be citable only if a tool registered it.
  • Examples:
    • Processing SEC data across 30+ million documents using citation registries.
  • Terminology:
    • citation registry
    • streaming citation filter
    • determinism
  • Why it matters: Ensures absolute verifiability and auditability of all numerical outputs.

Search and Reranking Strategy

  • Explanation: Combining Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) vector search with BM25 keyword search, followed by multi-stage reranking to ensure precise source retrieval.
  • Key claims:
    • Vector and BM25 searches run concurrently, over-fetching to top K.
    • Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) combines search results.
    • A trusted cross-encoder reranks results to filter out conflicting disclosures across documents.
  • Examples:
    • Resolving discrepancies between earnings call transcripts and 10-K filings.
  • Terminology:
    • ANN
    • BM25
    • Reciprocal Rank Fusion
    • cross-encoder
  • Why it matters: Ensures high recall and precision when querying vast unstructured and structured enterprise data.

Tenant Isolation and Security

  • Explanation: Enterprise AI requires strict document-level security to prevent data leakage between different users and internal datasets.
  • Key claims:
    • Every search hit is re-authorized in Postgres across tenant identity, ownership, and document access.
    • Builders add tenant filters dynamically to queries.
    • Only the auth subsystem can create scoped tokens.
  • Examples:
    • Preventing Citadel Desk 1 from accessing Citadel Desk 2's research.
  • Terminology:
    • tenant isolation
    • scoped token
    • post-authorization
  • Why it matters: Protects sensitive internal documents, SharePoint files, OneDrive data, and proprietary financial models from unauthorized access.

Key Points

The model plans; deterministic software handles every number

  • Explanation: LLMs should never write raw numbers directly. They produce plans and tool calls, while deterministic code executes math and formatting.
  • Evidence: Kepler's production data showing thousands of rejected citations due to mismatches.
  • Practical implication: Reduces hallucination rates to zero for numerical output generation.

Streaming citation filter strips unverified numbers mid-stream

  • Explanation: If a generated number cannot be matched against a registered source in the citation registry, the filter strips it during generation.
  • Evidence: Over 10,981 citations refused by the filter in production tests.
  • Practical implication: Guarantees that users never see unverified or hallucinated figures.

Traditional RAG is insufficient for numerical accuracy

  • Explanation: Standard vector database retrieval combined with unstructured LLM prompting fails at auditing, math, and scaling.
  • Evidence: A third of citations in naive RAG setups are unverified math or incorrect source lookups.
  • Practical implication: Engineers building financial or audit AI must adopt hybrid structured-unstructured registries.

Frameworks, Models & Processes

Kepler Numerical Verification Framework

  • How it works: Separates LLM generation from deterministic data retrieval, computation, and citation filtering.
  • Components:
    • LLM Agent (Plan generation)
    • Tools (Retrieval and computation)
    • Citation Registry (Typed sources and anchors)
    • Streaming Citation Filter (Post-processing verification)
  • When to use: Building enterprise AI applications requiring high numerical accuracy, auditing, and financial reporting.

Examples & Case Studies

Processing Apple's FY2025 revenue and growth rate calculation.

  • Illustrates: How clicking on a citation chip reveals the exact filing text, spreadsheet cell, and deterministic calculation steps behind every percentage and dollar figure.
  • Lesson: Traceability builds user trust and ensures complete auditability in financial AI.

Actionable Takeaways

  • Immediate:
    • Never trust raw LLM output for financial figures.
    • Implement post-processing citation filters on generation streams.
  • Strategic:
    • Combine vector search, BM25, and cross-encoder reranking for robust retrieval.
    • Enforce tenant isolation at the database level for all retrieval operations.
  • Questions to investigate:
    • How can smaller open-source models be adapted for strict citation planning?
    • What are the latency overheads of streaming citation filters in production?

Claims Worth Verifying

  • A third of all citations in financial LLM tasks are math the model did not actually do. (statistical)
  • The streaming filter refused 10,981 citations in production tests. (empirical)

Notable Quotes

"Do Not Let Models Invent Numbers" (at 0:12) "An analyst never shows a client a number they cannot trace." (at 2:24) "The model cites numbers. It never writes them." (at 6:42)

Compressed Summary

  • LLMs are probability machines unsuited for standalone numerical accuracy.
  • Kepler uses deterministic code and citation registries to verify every number.
  • Streaming filters strip unverified citations mid-stream to eliminate hallucinations.
  • Tenant isolation ensures strict data security across public and private enterprise namespaces.
  • Keywords: citations, hallucination, reranking, determinism, finance
  • Core insight: To eliminate financial hallucinations, AI systems must separate LLM planning from deterministic retrieval, computation, and citation filtering.

- **Evidence**: A third of citations in naive RAG setups are unverified math or incorrect source lookups.
- **Practical implication**: Engineers building financial or audit AI must adopt hybrid structured-unstructured registries.
## Frameworks, Models & Processes
### Kepler Numerical Verification Framework
- **How it works**: Separates LLM generation from deterministic data retrieval, computation, and citation filtering.
- **Components**:
  - LLM Agent (Plan generation)
  - Tools (Retrieval and computation)
  - Citation Registry (Typed sources and anchors)
  - Streaming Citation Filter (Post-processing verification)
- **When to use**: Building enterprise AI applications requiring high numerical accuracy, auditing, and financial reporting.
## Examples & Case Studies
### Processing Apple's FY2025 revenue and growth rate calculation.
- **Illustrates**: How clicking on a citation chip reveals the exact filing text, spreadsheet cell, and deterministic calculation steps behind every percentage and dollar figure.
- **Lesson**: Traceability builds user trust and ensures complete auditability in financial AI.
## Actionable Takeaways
- **Immediate**:
  - Never trust raw LLM output for financial figures.
  - Implement post-processing citation filters on generation streams.
- **Strategic**:
  - Combine vector search, BM25, and cross-encoder reranking for robust retrieval.
  - Enforce tenant isolation at the database level for all retrieval operations.
- **Questions to investigate**:
  - How can smaller open-source models be adapted for strict citation planning?
  - What are the latency overheads of streaming citation filters in production?
## Claims Worth Verifying
- A third of all citations in financial LLM tasks are math the model did not actually do. (statistical)
- The streaming filter refused 10,981 citations in production tests. (empirical)
## Notable Quotes
> "Do Not Let Models Invent Numbers" (at 0:12)
> "An analyst never shows a client a number they cannot trace." (at 2:24)
> "The model cites numbers. It never writes them." (at 6:42)
## Compressed Summary
- LLMs are probability machines unsuited for standalone numerical accuracy.
- Kepler uses deterministic code and citation registries to verify every number.
- Streaming filters strip unverified citations mid-stream to eliminate hallucinations.
- Tenant isolation ensures strict data security across public and private enterprise namespaces.
- **Keywords**: citations, hallucination, reranking, determinism, finance
- **Core insight**: To eliminate financial hallucinations, AI systems must separate LLM planning from deterministic retrieval, computation, and citation filtering.
